problem: Robot navigation typically relies on explicit geometric maps, which does not match how humans give and follow navigation directions expressed through semantic structure in natural language.
motivation: Human environments have rich semantic structure (corridors, doors, intersections, rooms) that people use to describe routes. Exploiting it could let robots follow natural-language directions without building a geometric map of the world.
key_idea: Represent navigation as a sequence of semantic behaviors and translate natural language instructions into behavior sequences that a robot executes without an explicit geometric world model.
